subject: Service notice: elevated 5xx/timeouts impacting rw-model-v3 - status & follow-up
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: support@skyapps.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service notice: elevated 5xx/timeouts impacting rw-model-v3 - initial alert

Hi Sara / SkyApps ops team,

We wanted to proactively notify you that between 08:50 - 09:05 PT we observed a spike in 5xx and timeout errors for requests routed to rw-model-v3 for your account (tenant: skyapps-prod). The spike affected ~4% of requests at peak and primarily surfaced on long-context requests (>2048 tokens).

What we know so far:
- Scope: SkyApps production traffic routed to rw-model-v3 in us-west.
- Observable impact: elevated 5xx (internal server error) and backend timeouts; client-facing 504s for a subset of requests.
- Started: ~2026-06-30 08:50 PT; ongoing at time of this message.

Immediate mitigations we're applying now:
- Routing: we are automatically routing new requests to rw-model-v2 for queues where requests exceed 2s expected latency.
- Rate control: a temporary soft rate limit is applied to high-concurrency clients to reduce queuing.
- Investigation: Dev is investigating kernel/runtime selection anomalies that correlate with certain sequence length distributions.

Attached: sample error logs we captured (rw-v3-error-sample-logs.txt).

Action requested from you:
- If you can, send any request IDs or example payloads that correlate to errors on your side (reply with the IDs or attach logs). That helps us map client-side traces to server logs.

We’ll follow up with status updates and an ETA for full recovery. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your users and we’re focused on restoring normal service.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@skyapps.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:28:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Service notice: elevated 5xx/timeouts impacting rw-model-v3 - initial alert

Thanks for the heads up, Ava.

We started seeing 500s at 08:55 PT and they look consistent with the times you mentioned. Sample request IDs from our side: req_20260630_4412, req_20260630_4431. We can pull full request/response traces if that helps; want to confirm if you need those.

Quick Qs:
- Any ETA on when routing to rw-model-v2 will be in effect for all our traffic?
- Will there be any changes to tokenization or output that could affect downstream processing?

Thanks — Sara
Sara Nguyen
Head of Ops, SkyApps Inc.
sara.nguyen@skyapps.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@skyapps.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:47:06 -0700
Subject: Re: Service notice: elevated 5xx/timeouts impacting rw-model-v3 - initial alert

Sara — thanks for the IDs, those are helpful. I pulled the server traces matching req_20260630_4412 and req_20260630_4431 and attached a short excerpt.

Preliminary technical summary (observed):
- Pattern: errors cluster on requests that have prompt+history lengths between 2050–2300 tokens.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): a kernel selection regression in the v3 quantized execution path under a recent runtime optimization. For this sequence-length band, the runtime chose a less memory-fragmentation-friendly kernel which caused transient OOM/retry loops and backend timeouts.
- Impact: ~4% of rw-model-v3 requests across multiple tenants in us-west; SkyApps was impacted more due to a higher fraction of long-context requests.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
1) Forced routing: we’ve applied a tenant-level routing rule so incoming SkyApps rw-model-v3 requests are redirected to rw-model-v2 while we validate fixes (this is live).
2) Reverted the kernel-selection optimization in the canary pool which mitigated the issue for instances processed there.
3) Increased KV cache headroom for affected hosts to reduce pressure during retries.

Next steps we’re executing now:
- Run a focused test suite for the quantized v3 path across sequence-length slices (in progress).
- If tests pass, we’ll roll out a patch to the v3 runtime in canary and then a staged rollout to production.

We expect to have a recovery ETA within ~2–3 hours (targeting 12:30–13:00 PT for wider stability), and will update you when we start the rollout. If you can share full traces for the two IDs, please attach them.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Service notice: elevated 5xx/timeouts impacting rw-model-v3 - recovery update + draft RCA

Sara — quick status. We hit our recovery milestone at ~12:45 PT and error rates have returned to baseline (<0.1%). The tenant-level routing to rw-model-v2 remained in place during the mitigation window.

What we rolled out:
- Reverted the kernel-selection optimization across the production pool and pushed a conservative configuration to the v3 runtime that avoids the problematic kernel for 2k+ token inputs.
- Applied the canary-tested change to all affected hosts; we monitored for regressions for 30m before lifting the tenant redirect.

Timeline (summary):
- 08:50 PT — first elevated errors observed.
- 09:00 PT — routing to rw-model-v2 for SkyApps enabled; investigation begins.
- 09:30–11:45 PT — focused testing and rollback in canaries.
- 12:30–12:45 PT — staged rollout completed; monitoring shows recovery.

Attached: postmortem draft (postmortem-draft-2026-07-01.pdf) and a short playbook snippet we used for the rollback (recovery-playbook-snippet.txt).

We do not expect tokenization or output differences between rw-model-v3 and the fallback v2 for your usage pattern; we validated that the response format and length distribution stayed within acceptable bounds during a short test.

Next steps:
- We’ll finalize and share an RCA doc with a more detailed timeline and proposed mitigations (kernel selection telemetry, additional sequence-length guards, and improved staging tests).
- Offer: we’d like to propose a service credit for the impacted window; I can put together numbers if that would be helpful.

Please let us know if you want a short sync (15–20 min) to walk through the postmortem or review the mitigation plan.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll continue to monitor.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@skyapps.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final postmortem and remediation plan — rw-model-v3 2026-06-30 incident

Hi Sara / SkyApps team,

Following up with the final postmortem and remediation plan now that we completed our internal validation. Thank you for the quick traces — they were useful in narrowing the window.

Executive summary:
- Incident: transient elevated 5xx/timeouts for rw-model-v3 driven by an aggressive kernel-selection optimization interacting poorly with quantized execution on requests ~2050–2300 tokens.
- Impact: SkyApps experienced ~4% elevated error rate for a 55-minute window; overall platform impact limited to us-west production pool.
- Root cause: insufficient staging coverage for the quantized execution path across the long-context slice; a regression allowed a memory-fragmenting kernel to be selected.

Remediations and timeline:
1) Fix: patch to kernel-selection logic that adds an explicit sequence-length guard — deployed 2026-07-01 (complete).
2) Testing: added long-context slice to automated canary tests and created a targeted stress job (in QA this week).
3) Telemetry: new metric and alert for kernel-selection anomalies and memory-fragmentation signals (ETA: 2 weeks).
4) Process: expanded rollout windows and mandatory canary window for core runtime changes (immediate).

Compensation: Ava will follow up on a service credit proposal for the impacted window.

Attached: final postmortem PDF (postmortem-draft-2026-07-01.pdf) and relevant logs (rw-v3-error-sample-logs.txt). We can schedule a 20–30 min review session if you prefer.

Apologies again for the disruption. We appreciate the rapid coordination and the traces you sent — they materially shortened the RCA.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
